entities.summary: Pierre Paulin was a French furniture designer and interior designer. His uncle, Georges Paulin, was a part-time automobile designer and invented the mechanical retractable hardtop, who was later executed by the Nazis in 1941 as a hero of the French Resistance. After failing his Baccalauréat, Paulin trained as a ceramist in Vallaurius on the French Riviera and later as a stone‑carver in Burgundy. Soon after, he injured his right arm in a fight, which ended his hopes of becoming a sculptor. He then attended the École Camondo in Paris.
